# Vendor-owned sources behind the `verified` field of the POLICY literals (ticket Q8c, PR 1).
# A kind module names a source by its id only; this file resolves the id. No URL is written in src/.
# What the files are: documentation source files (the files the vendors' pages are built from; the rendered
# pages were not reachable) and four source-code files (K-SRC, V-ACL, V-PARSE, B-ACL). 19 rows.
# Who read what:
# - Rows V-POL to K-SRC (16 rows): a separate evidence runner read them on 2026-11-11 between 14:02 and
#   14:20 UTC and recorded which permission names and path forms it found (it saved no text and no hash).
# - The one-part wildcard `+` of grant R17 (V-POL, B-POL, V-ACL, V-PARSE, B-ACL) and the paths `undelete`,
#   `subkeys` and `byok-export` were read by the builder of fix batch 1 on 2026-11-11 about 15:35 UTC, not by
#   the evidence runner. Nobody else has re-read them yet.
# Who produced each sha256:
# - The 16 rows V-POL to K-SRC: the first builder fetched each file at 14:30 UTC and hashed the bytes. The
#   evidence runner fetched all 16 again about 15:30 UTC and got the same hashes (handover evidence
#   Q8c-1/7af1380/source-hashes.txt). The Kubernetes rows named a branch then; the same bytes are at the
#   commits now written here (checked by the second builder at 15:38 UTC).
# - V-ACL, V-PARSE, B-ACL: fetched and hashed by the second builder only, at 15:35 UTC. Not re-fetched by
#   anyone else yet.
# Every row is pinned: the commit column is a commit id and it is written in the URL. The 7 Vault documentation
# rows (V-POL to V-K8S) carry a 7-character id: the full 40-character id could not be looked up from this
# session (the GitHub API refused the request), so it is NOT written here and was not guessed. The other 12 rows
# carry full 40-character ids.
# Versions: Vault source code (V-ACL, V-PARSE) is the commit the tag v2.2.0 pointed to, the version the engine
# tests run against (hashicorp/vault:2.2.0). OpenBao source code (B-ACL) is the commit the tag v2.4.0 pointed
# to. The OpenBao documentation rows (B-POL, B-KV, B-TR, B-API) are at commit 0d706a0c...; which OpenBao release
# that commit belongs to was not looked up, so the OpenBao claims are not tied to one release.
# WHAT A LATER EVIDENCE RUNNER MUST RE-READ (2026-11-11): only the items listed below were read by the builder
# of a fix alone (the other readings are the evidence runner's, named above). Each has a dated entry in
# tools/policy_page.py (review by the earliest review date the page names; `python tools/policy_page.py --check` and the tests run the rule).
# - V-POL and B-POL: the passage that says `+` matches exactly one path segment in a policy path.
# - V-ACL and B-ACL: the code that matches a policy path with `+` (a whole path part, nothing deeper, and what
#   a `+` does to the longest-prefix choice).
# - V-PARSE: the code that reads a policy path and refuses `+*`.
# - B-ACL: the same matching rule in OpenBao.
# - V-KV and B-KV: the paths `undelete`, `subkeys` (and `byok-export` in V-TR and B-TR). Nobody has read the
#   passage that says a `read` on a secret's path also serves a request for an older version (grant R17).
# - V-TR and B-TR: that the exact signing path (`sign/<key>`) does not also allow the longer path that ends in a
#   hash algorithm name (grant R18). Nobody has read this yet.
# - K-AUTHZ and K-RBAC: that the query parameters the Kubernetes code sends (`limit`, `continue`, `timestamps`,
#   `sinceTime`, `limitBytes`) do not change the verb a request needs (grants R20 to R22). Nobody has read this
#   yet.
# - K-SSRR and K-AUTHZ: that `create` on the three self-review resources (`selfsubjectrulesreviews`,
#   `selfsubjectaccessreviews`, `selfsubjectreviews`) writes nothing (the Kubernetes free request
#   `k8s.rules_review` and the never-list line `create`). K-SSRR describes only the first resource and does not
#   mention the verb. Nobody has read this yet.
# After that run: set `claims_unverified` of R17, R18 and R20 to R22 back to () and delete their PENDING_CLAIMS
# entries; do the same for the Kubernetes free request and the never-list line `create`; set `verified` of the three never-list paths in the kind modules and delete their PENDING_NAMES
# entries (both dictionaries are in tools/policy_page.py). The hashes of V-ACL,
# V-PARSE and B-ACL must be fetched again at the same time (nobody has re-fetched them).
# No test fetches anything or compares a hash: the hashes are a record for a person to re-check.
# The two lines below are read by tools/policy_page.py: the page marks these ids. A test checks that every id named
# in the list above (V-... B-... K-...) is on one of them.
# BUILDER-ONLY: V-ACL, V-PARSE, B-ACL
# PARTLY-BUILDER-ONLY: V-POL, B-POL, V-KV, B-KV, V-TR, B-TR, K-AUTHZ, K-RBAC, K-SSRR
# Two more lines, read by tools/policy_page.py: which claim (a statement in `claims_unverified` of a kind module)
# has which mark on the page. A claim is named by its FULL text: the whole text must be equal, the start of a text
# is not enough. Several texts are separated by ` ;; ` (a space, two semicolons, a space); two semicolons may not
# stand inside a text. "builder read the passage": the builder of a fix read the vendor passage behind the claim;
# no evidence runner has. "nobody has read the passage": nobody has found the passage. Only the claim about the
# `+` of grant R17 (sources V-POL, B-POL, V-ACL, V-PARSE, B-ACL) has a builder-read passage; every other claim
# (6 different texts) is nobody-read. Of the 9 ids on the PARTLY-BUILDER-ONLY line only V-POL and B-POL have a
# builder-read passage behind a claim; for the other 7 (V-KV, B-KV, V-TR, B-TR, K-AUTHZ, K-RBAC, K-SSRR) the passage
# behind the claim is read by nobody (in V-KV, B-KV, V-TR and B-TR the builder read a path name, listed above, not a
# claim). The page head lists both sets of claims in full, built from these two lines. A claim with no text here, or
# whose text is on both lines, fails the data check; so does a builder-read mark on a claim whose entry names none of
# the BUILDER-ONLY sources (the mark would be on the wrong claim).
# CLAIM-READ-BY-BUILDER: the + matches exactly one whole path part, nothing deeper
# CLAIM-READ-BY-NOBODY: a `read` on a secret's path also serves a request for an older version of that secret ;; the exact path R18 does not also allow Vault's longer sign path that ends in a hash algorithm name ;; the query parameters `limit` and `continue` do not change the verb the request needs ;; the query parameters `timestamps`, `sinceTime` and `limitBytes` do not change the verb the request needs ;; a `create` on `selfsubjectrulesreviews` changes nothing in the cluster (the one source for the resource, K-SSRR, does not say so) ;; `create` on `selfsubjectrulesreviews`, `selfsubjectaccessreviews` and `selfsubjectreviews` writes nothing (the source for the first, K-SSRR, does not mention the verb; none was found for the other two)
